Issued at 314 AM EDT Wed Aug 26 2026

PATTERN SYNOPSIS/FORECAST:

Broad ridge axis restrengthening over the PacNW...as 568dm 500mb low 
swirls over western Manitoba near the MN border, resulting difluence 
over the Upper Midwest and parts of Ontario...with a second PV max 
digging south into northern Manitoba attm, and a slight bit of a 
warm nose/wraparound moisture between these two features. Wad of 
moisture beneath the swirly across the Midwest/Ontario, with pwats 
generally ranging from 1.2 to 1.5 in, highest right ahead of a 
niblet of energy swinging across the western UP as of 3z where some 
convection has been taking place...and is becoming somewhat 
disconnected from greater wad of deep moisture from the Mid MS 
Valley/Central Plains down into the Gulf Coast...with splitting flow 
in the mid/low levels in this area. Warm, moist advection across the 
Upper Midwest on SW/SSW low-level flow...slowly pressing eastward 
across WI and the central Yoop. Surface reflection of the upper 
swirly is an occluded low positioned over western Ontario, with a 
cold front draped from here down to KS...and warm front stretching 
toward the Keweenaw and central Lake Superior as of 0z. A second 
cold front drapes from ND to Hudson Bay, just behind aforementioned 
low...with stronger northerly flow over central Canada. 

Shortwave trough swings across the Upper Great Lakes today with 
attendant surface system and convection; lobe over northern Manitoba 
punches SSE into the Lower Great Lakes and scrapes us Thursday into 
Friday. Heights try to build eastward into the Upper Midwest going 
into the end of the week with increasing warm advection out of the 
Plains...with decreasing influence from upper low that looks to 
strengthen over eastern Canada. Another bit of PV tracks near the 
US/Canadian border this weekend into early next week (timing a 
little unclear attm), and attm appears to track just to our north, 
with a pattern shift in the works as troughing digs into western 
North America for a change. This idea, if it holds, would indicate 
potential for a warming trend across the eastern US toward the 
middle-end of next week...though we still have a lot of time between 
now and then to see how things change. 


FORECAST DETAILS...

Heavy rain potential today...think the setup remains favorable for 
heavy rain, with pwats up toward 1.5in, freezing levels up around 
700mb or so, and lack of flow likely leading to slower storm 
motions/longer potential for residence time over an area. Currently, 
still expect the heaviest rain (potential for greater than an inch) 
will be across the EUP closer to the better synoptic forcing, and 
perhaps NE Lower as we go into the afternoon/evening with potential 
for a couple rounds of storms and perhaps a bit more of an E-W 
component to the flow, a little more parallel to the boundary. 
Naturally, any storms will be capable of producing localized heavy 
rainfall, and thus, there could be some hotter spots outside of the 
aforementioned areas. 

Severe storm potential today...Finally starting to see some 
convective development closer to our area by 7z, along/ahead of a 
couple boundaries that have been tracking eastward across WI all 
night...perhaps even a shallow outflow boundary crossing N Lower 
during the 6z hour, per a subtle N-S line in radar reflectivity near 
Kalkaska/Bellaire. Anyway, this suggests we are finally starting to 
destabilize, and will therefore need to keep a close eye on the next 
3-6, 4-8hrs, with this first round of warm-advective showers and 
storms moving through. Think the better axis of instability is to 
our southwest, though, and think this will likely stay to our 
southwest (per a redeveloping line near ARX early this morning, 
tracking along the thickness gradient across southern WI). Would not 
be entirely surprised if all of this ended up splitting and focusing 
more to the north across the EUP and more toward GRR today, but will 
see. Better instability reaches us around 12-15z into the remainder 
of the afternoon, though based on guidance soundings, it may remain 
mostly elevated for quite some time, with a warm nose in the mid-
levels...and we may struggle to actually get typical surface based 
CAPE in many areas till perhaps late afternoon...except for perhaps 
our southeast corner where there is a better shot at breaks in the 
clouds and diurnal heating. (Interestingly, soundings across parts 
of the Yoop suggest that while we may warm enough to overcome the 
warm nose...it may remain too moist and stable in the low-levels for 
parcels to accelerate off the surface.) Attm, appears deep-layer 
shear increases this afternoon into this evening ahead of a front 
(or two) draping across the area, and this could allow for
